lead.claim: Digital monitoring with feedback boosts walking and balance after stroke at home.
lead.context: Why this matters: This RCT examined if a mobile-based monitoring system with clinician feedback improved outcomes for stroke survivors in home rehabilitation.

supporting.claim: Consider pelvic floor yoga for women with overactive bladder and leakage.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This subgroup analysis of an RCT investigated pelvic floor yoga compared to general physical conditioning for women with overactive bladder-wet.

supporting.claim: Multimodal stroke interventions may be less effective for patients aged 80 and older.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This RCT assessed the impact of age and frailty on a multimodal long-term intervention for stroke survivors.

supporting.claim: The pudendal nerve commonly presents as a single trunk but has anatomical variability.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This systematic review and meta-analysis described the anatomical variations and measurements of the pudendal nerve.

supporting.claim: A new control strategy makes FES cycling safer and more reproducible for SCI patients.
supporting.context: Why this matters: This study developed and validated a simulation-derived, synergy-based control strategy for functional electrical stimulation cycling in a person with spinal cord injury.
